provenance.notes: ONNX quantized requantization rounds ties to even; accumulators +/-1 and +/-5 with y_scale=2 produce exact +/-0.5 and +/-2.5 tie values.
A finite requantized value far outside the uint8 range should saturate; converting the rounded f32 to i32 before clamping can wrap.
A valid positive subnormal output scale can make small integer accumulators requantize beyond uint8; the result should saturate before any i32 conversion of an infinite f32.
Per-column quantization path with a valid positive subnormal output scale should saturate uint8 results before any i32 conversion of an infinite f32.
Batched rank-3 scalar quantization path with a valid positive subnormal output scale should saturate uint8 results before any i32 conversion of an infinite f32.
A batched (2x8x256 by 2x256x64) uint8 by int8 quantized matmul with a subnormal y_scale=1e-40 checks that the result saturates to the uint8 range [0,255] instead of overflowing or producing NaN.
Batched per-column quantization path with valid positive subnormal y_scale: large positive/negative requantized values should saturate before integer conversion.
Per-column B scale and zero point broadcast from batch 1 while A supplies two output batches; the GPU must use a zero batch stride for both quantization tensors.
Uses ORT QLinearMatMul3D_U8U8 values in a legal MatMul broadcast form where A is rank 2 and B is rank 3.
Uses ORT QLinearMatMul3D_U8S8 values in a legal MatMul broadcast form where A is rank 3 and B is rank 2.
Compact 4D MatMul broadcast extension of ORT's quantized matmul coverage.

Diverges from the upstream test's inputs (inputs.b constant 1 -> cycle [1, 3]); the expected output is recomputed by the CPU reference for the new inputs. On the fused DP4A path, every accumulator is 1 in even output columns and 3 in odd ones against y_scale=2, so ONNX round-half-to-even must send the exact halves 0.5 and 1.5 to their even neighbours 0 and 2.
Production-sized scalar-quantization case for the fused DP4A path: a valid positive subnormal y_scale should saturate large positive/negative requantized values before converting to integer.

Equal positive subnormal input/output scales cancel exactly. Requantization decodes their integer significands before float arithmetic can flush them, preserving the identity contraction [1, 2, 3, 4].
Empty-input subcase from QLinearMatMul2DTest(false).
With equal B and Y scales, the stored a_scale puts row 1, column 3 just beyond a negative half-integer tie, checking that ties-to-even rounding preserves the scale-product residual exactly.
An M=1 int8 GEMV with requantization and a one-lane K tail exercises the tileM=1 DP4A specialization. Column-varying B values expose dropped columns in both unrolled and scalar-tail reduction.
Aligned K=64 scalar-quantized matrix multiplication checks exact integer output across multiple rows and columns.
Per-column requantization with a one-element reduction tail checks exact integer output.
Reduction length 129 leaves one final element; scalar quantization parameters must still produce the exact output.
K=63 exercises scalar requantization with a three-lane packed reduction tail in the 32<=K<128 range.

Rank-4 signed-input matmul with an unsigned output and dimensions large enough for packed accumulation. Verifies that output dtype selection is independent of the input types while preserving batched broadcasting and output quantization.
A rank-1 left operand is promoted to a single row for the multiply and the promoted axis is removed from the result, so a vector times a matrix is a vector.
A rank-1 right operand is promoted to a single column and that axis is removed from the result, so a matrix times a vector is a vector.
Both operands rank 1: each promoted axis is removed, leaving a scalar result.
K=3 excludes aligned packed routes while both B scale and zero point are per-column. Exact binary scales exercise nonuniform output and ties-to-even requantization on the generic two-pass route.
Exact integer partials with reduction and output tails, per-column scales and mixed input/output signedness. Power-of-two scales exercise deterministic ties-to-even requantization.
Exact integer partials with reduction and output tails, per-column scales and mixed input/output signedness. Power-of-two scales exercise deterministic ties-to-even requantization.
Exact dot products +/-260000 with stored f32 scales produce +/-19.49999912828208 before the output zero point. Rounding the scale chain to a half tie changes one output unit.
Scalar B scale with per-column B zero points; mixed signedness, extreme zero points and M/N/K tails. Exact partial sums and unsaturated power-of-two requantization.

Alternating rows contract to +/-(2^24+1) and +/-(2^24-1); with a_scale=b_scale=1.0 and y_scale=33,554,432 (2^25), the exact output lands at 128 and 128+/-1, distinguishing half-integer neighbors without overflow (M=2, K=1038, N=4).

The same alternating-row contraction (+/-(2^24+1) and +/-(2^24-1)) with a_scale=2.98e-8 (2^-25) and b_scale=y_scale=0.125 reproduces the identical 128 and 128+/-1 output, checking that requantization stays exact when the scale is split differently (M=2, K=1038, N=4).

The same alternating-row contraction scaled to a 32x1038 by 1038x64 matrix (a_scale=b_scale=1.0, y_scale=33,554,432) repeats the 128 and 128+/-1 pattern across every column, checking requantization correctness at matrix width.
